newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Meredith sees FY97 revenue rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Meredith sees FY97 revenue rise.

text.p: Meredith Corp expects mid-single-digit revenue growth in fiscal 1997 when all discontinued assets are taken into account, said Jack Rehm, chairman and chief executive officer.

"I think it's probably going to be in the middle single-digits, and in this climate, that's not too bad," Rehm said in a telephone interview, adding "we'll certainly improve our margins in the process."
The Des Moines, Iowa-based magazine and television company had revenues of $867.1 million for fiscal 1996 ended June 30.
Some analysts had projected flat revenue growth in fiscal 1997 for Meredith.
But Rehm said, "On an apples-to-apples basis, it's not a flat revenue picture. Remember, we've eliminated $50 million in revenue by either disposing of assets or shutting down products."

In discussing the recently completed first quarter, Rehm said he was "very comfortable" with the First Call analyst earnings estimate consensus of $0.42 per share. In the year-ago period, Meredith earned $0.34 per share.

"Paper costs have returned to be quite favorable for magazine publishers. The (paper) market has softened," Rehm said, predicting the favorable environment will prevail through the end of the calendar year.

During the current second quarter, Rehm reiterated that Meredith expects to record a net gain of about $15 million to $20 million from the previously announced sale of its cable television systems interests, marking its exit from that segment.
The executive said Meredith seeks to expand its television broadcasting holdings, which now total seven stations.
While the company has explored television acquisition possibilities, Rehm said, "It's a tough market, and prices are high in the top 40 markets."
Meredith's stock traded Monday at 49-1/2, up 1/4.
